He experienced anguish, through which he obtained tranquility. "Falling was originally just another name for flying." And on this eighth day, he granted himself "departure."
short_text: He once dreamed of being the sun but fell to earth, finding pain and tranquility in his descent.

raw_text: Looking back at her childhood, she remembered the first time she heard adventure stories of the Trailblaze. During those lonely times, towering stacks of books, scattered engine blueprints, and empty bottles of paint became her everyday life. Her frail figure wielded the brush, carefully outlining the dream she yearned for. "Perhaps I can seize more possibilities within this limited time." Carrying the wish she shared with her friend, she became the person she had always dreamed of becoming. "The journey of the Trailblaze begins at this very moment." short_text: From a sickbed to the stars, she painted her dreams of a comet ship and silver rail, turning her childhood wish into a journey of the Trailblaze.

"Then they can choose a more fitting king by that time. I won't protest." "But what if such a person will never exist?" "...Then I'll do my best to meet everyone's expectations." Now, the girl had long since become aware of how profound that tragedy would be. Would she have chosen to give up if she were to return to that moment where everything began? The king does not speak and simply grasps the sword tightly. The stone again gives out a thundering roar as the sword is pulled out.
short_text: Altria accepts her fate as king, vowing to meet everyone's expectations despite the thankless task, as she pulls the sword from the stone.

name: After the Charmony Fall

raw_text: The eternal dream he longed for vanished in an instant. As he plummeted towards the earth, he felt no sadness; only a desire to close his eyes. And why do they wake? — As planets streak past outside the wind, this answer now demands a new meaning to be given. "Maybe... just maybe I still can..."
short_text: As he falls through the sky, a traveler from the past clings to hope, carrying the weight of a vanished dream and the eternal cycle of suffering. Why do people slumber and wake, and can he find a new meaning in the stars?

name: Along the Passing Shore
subtitle: 5★ Light Cone · Nihility
raw_text: Flowing in the narrow border between “existence” and “nothingness”, the ice-cold tides eternally lap against the shores and bring all things to their final end. In this place, the drowned ask for help, lament with songs, find their happiness, enjoy sweet moments, and suffer great agony… All these are reflected in the water. She cannot experience these, but she can feel them– There are still many roads to walk, many sounds to listen to, and many things to change before she arrives at the end. She reaches out and saves the drowning from the temptations of Nihility, and one mirage after another bursts apart behind her figure. She keeps walking in this boundless world, all for an end that does not exist. – And it’s always raining here.
short_text: In a liminal realm where ice meets nothingness, a figure walks on forever, saving the drowning from Nihilistic mirages, all while the rain never stops.

subtitle: 4★ Light Cone · Nihility
raw_text: Their dance glides gracefully, shadows and light silently exchanging places. She takes the other person's hand, her smile beaming into those indifferent eyes. "Beautiful Ranger... Panic-stricken, she tries to withdraw her hand, falling backward. The surroundings brighten again, the banquet's clamor resurfacing. Her dance partner gently supports her waist, as if oblivious to the ordeal that just unfolded. "What a lovely dance that was, Memokeeper. Shall we have another go?"

short_text: Helektra dances through the seas, her crimson blade singing the lament of life as she searches for an audience in the starry expanse.

name: Yet Hope Is Priceless
subtitle: 5★ Light Cone · Erudition
raw_text: "Lady Bonajade, if it weren't for your continuous supply of goods and donations, the orphanage would probably..." She gently stroked the children's heads, cutting off the director's words.
